messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High latency observed for tenant AceroMed in dedicated-us-west pool. P99 token latency > 2.5s for last 5m. Paging on-call.

jhayes: acked, taking. Looking at queues + scheduler metrics.

maria_g: I can join — saw customer pulse on our dashboard, throughput spike ~3x baseline. Are they running a batch scoring job?

eng_mike: they pushed a large ingest job around 08:12 UTC, lots of long-context generations. max_batch_tokens for that tenant is currently 1024.

jhayes: confirmed. Scheduler shows many giant batches forming -> long tail. Also queue depth spiked to 1200 requests. CPU on pool nodes fine but GPU latency climbs with big batches.

sre_claire: tagging possible mitigations: 1) apply tenant-level max_batch_tokens cap (e.g., 256) 2) enable per-tenant queue_depth cap 3) temporarily route tenant to isolated pool or reduce batch_wait_ms.

maria_g: we should prefer a non-disruptive quick knob first — set max_batch_tokens down to 256 and lower max_batch_wait_ms to 25ms for this tenant. That reduces tail without moving them.

jhayes: agree. Preparing a safe change. Will push a per-tenant override via runtime API.

eng_mike: FYI, their model variant is gpt-open-7b-quant. It's stable under smaller batches. No need to change model.

jhayes: executing CLI patch:

```
redwoodctl runtime override set --tenant acero-med --pool dedicated-us-west \
  --max_batch_tokens 256 --max_batch_wait_ms 25 --note "emergency tail mitigation"
```

ops-bot: Change queued. Applying to 4 serving groups.

incident-bot: CHANGE: override apply started (id: ov-2026-03-15-01).

jhayes: applied to 2/4 groups, applying rolling to remaining groups. Monitoring p99.

sre_claire: also add short-lived circuit-breaker: tenant_queue_max_inflight=200 to prevent head-of-line blocking.

jhayes: adding that now.

```
redwoodctl runtime override set --tenant acero-med --tenant_queue_max_inflight 200
```

ops-bot: override applied to all groups.

maria_g: p50/p90 improved already, p99 dropped from 2.6s -> 860ms in 90s. Great.

cs_renee: cs on standby to message AceroMed. Can we confirm whether any requests were dropped or errored?

eng_mike: error rate peaked at 0.8%, now back to baseline 0.05%. No 5xx spikes. Mostly latency.

cs_renee: OK, I'll draft an incident notice. Want to be transparent about us throttling batch tokens temporarily and working on long-term config.

jhayes: can someone run a light load-test to validate stability before I hand off? small synthetic with long context to mimic their job.

sre_claire: I'll run a 5-minute test from canary region against dedicated-us-west with the override.

(5m later)

sre_claire: test done: sustained 2k rps with mixed lengths. p99 remains ~900-1.1s, acceptable. No node OOMs.

maria_g: suggestion for long-term: create a tenant profile for AceroMed with: max_batch_tokens=512 for scheduled large jobs, tenant_queue_max_inflight=300, and a scheduled maintenance window to move heavy scoring to offpeak or to a private pool. Also consider advising customer to use chunking for long contexts.

jhayes: noted. I'll open a follow-up runbook ticket and link to this thread.

cs_renee: sent preliminary note to AceroMed AMs: "We've applied temporary batching limits to reduce latency; no data loss; we're coordinating longer-term options."

eng_mike: also recommend we add a runtime metric alert: per-tenant max_batch_tokens > 512 triggers warning — to catch future dangerous configs.

jhayes: handing off to night on-call @maria_g. Summary for handoff:
- Incident: P99 latency spike for AceroMed due to oversized batches after ingest job.
- Actions taken: per-tenant max_batch_tokens reduced to 256, max_batch_wait_ms=25, tenant_queue_max_inflight=200 (rolled to all serving groups).
- Impact: latency improved, error rate minimal. Customer not impacted functionally.
- Next steps: open runbook ticket + customer profile, consider scheduled dedicated window or pool if they keep heavy jobs.

maria_g: thanks — taking. I'll monitor for next 6h and coordinate with CS for a scheduled remediation call tomorrow.

jhayes: thanks team. tagging incident-bot to close the page if metrics remain stable.

incident-bot: RESOLVE CHECK: p99 for AceroMed < 1.2s for 5m — condition met. Paging will be resolved in 5s unless new alerts fire.

ops-bot: ov-2026-03-15-01: mark temporary overrides (max_batch_tokens, tenant_queue_max_inflight) with TTL=12h and owner=maria_g.

cs_renee: adding note to customer-facing incident doc and scheduling a follow-up. :white_check_mark:

maria_g: one last action item — create an eval to quantify quality difference at 256 vs 1024 for their primary prompt set. I'll own it.

eng_mike: thanks, all. Closing thread after runbook link posted.

jhayes: runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/INC-1772004000-bespoke-batching (will link), handing off.

maria_g: night team, ping me if anything flares.

(reacts: :thumbsup: from eng_mike, :pray: from cs_renee)
